prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: advisory-only; human authority/verification; no autonomous dispatch/control/release. Mandatory segmentation/time-sync/health-checks/audit-logging; observations timestamp/georeference/equipment-status; coordination records timestamp/participants/radio-path-status. Actors: local fire agencies, county emergency management, state wildland fire resources, aviation support units, cooperating public safety partners; command staff. Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): Duty Detection Officer (Orion) reviews Thermal Spot Snippet; searchable advance/hold/dismiss reasons; no suppression-assignment/public-notification. County Emergency Liaison manages dispatch/roads/evacuation/notifications; sends Drone Corridor Permit after jurisdiction review; constraints enter Portal before briefing. North Lookout Camera Mast sends Thermal Spot Snippet, timestamped smoke-bearing/pan/tilt/zoom/confidence; South Lookout Camera Mast supplies independent bearing track and Camera Cleaning Log; triangulate origin/uncertainty; assess visibility. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): launch/recovery/charging/shelter/health/security; maintenance triggers Battery Swap Ticket. Drone Tasking Service packages approved imaging footprints/altitude-bands/revisit-intervals; shall avoid active aviation lanes. Drone Pilot Operator verifies routes/safety/compliance; ticket aligns endurance/return-time. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): traceable fusion; may down-weight degraded Smoke Classifier Module, which produces Ridge Shadow Mask, smoke-likelihood/growth-trend/obscuration. Scores cannot declare fire. Confirmation requires persistent smoke/thermal plus independent corroboration or recorded authorized visual judgment; deficient evidence remains triaged. Confirmed Ignition State exposes location/confidence/history/reviewer/coordination-posture; delayed approval preserves planning, blocks dispatch. Airspace Restricted State requires authority-accepted restrictions. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): quality-checked weather, Wind Shift Bulletin, aviation wind/visibility. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold): lanes/status. Air Attack Supervisor (Redtail): route deconfliction before drone launch, restrictions/perimeter checks before release. Tanker Base Manager checks East Retardant Loading Pump/West Retardant Loading Pump; East produces Retardant Batch Slip after metering/sealing. Helitack Crew Leader uses Crewline Mobile Tablet: command-released information, instruction acknowledgements, crew-area reports; Portal displays beside tasks for clearance verification. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger):

New part:
S112: Analytic results are not displayed as final fireline until confidence thresholds, sensor age, and positional error are applied as explicit map attributes.
S113: The MesoWest Weather Fusion Node ingests station observations, forecast grids, and local quality checks to maintain the wind, humidity, temperature, and stability fields used by the spread model.
S114: Brindle publishes a time-indexed weather update that marks significant forecast changes and identifies which map products require recomputation.
S115: Weather fields are interpolated across the incident area with terrain-aware weighting so ridge, drainage, and slope effects are represented at operational map scale.
S116: Geospatial overlays include fuels, slope, aspect, roads, structures, water sources, jurisdiction boundaries, evacuation zones, and known communications coverage.
S117: The fire behavior model combines the accepted perimeter, recent growth vectors, weather fields, and fuel conditions to estimate short-term spread direction and rate.
S118: Model output is expressed as probability bands rather than a single line so supervisors can see both the most likely path and the practical planning margin.
S119: Emberhall renders the current perimeter, projected spread, resource positions, and decision annotations into a common operating picture with role-based symbology.
S120: The Caldera Incident Command Portal produces the Crew Staging Pin from the approved map layer and assigns it an effective time, location accuracy, and incident identifier.
S121: Operational recommendations are generated from rule checks that compare projected fire arrival times with values at risk, road access, crew travel time, and aircraft availability.
S122: Recommendations may include confirming an ignition, increasing camera monitoring, requesting drone coverage, preparing aviation options, repositioning ground crews, or notifying county partners.
S123: The Air Attack Supervisor receives map products that emphasize projected columns, flight hazards, target areas, and timing constraints without obscuring ground resource information.
S124: The County Emergency Liaison receives a simplified view that preserves perimeter confidence, threatened areas, and recommended public safety coordination actions while hiding tactical details not needed for civil coordination.
S125: Every map product records source time, processing time, model version, analyst acceptance, and supersession status so users can distinguish current guidance from archived assessments.
S126: When inputs conflict, the common operating picture shows the conflict explicitly and requires review before the affected recommendation is promoted for command use.
S127: Suppression planning begins after the Caldera Incident Command Portal promotes an accepted fire location into the operational map and marks it available for aviation review.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
